beginner.headline: Almost 1,000 Arrested After Mass Protests in France
beginner.brief: Hundreds of thousands of people protested across France on Saturday. They marched because the cost of living is very high. The protests were mostly peaceful during the day. Clashes between police and protesters happened late on Saturday. Police officers used tear gas to stop the crowds. Officials said that police arrested almost 1,000 people. People also protested in other European countries for similar reasons.

intermediate.headline: Mass Protests Across France Lead to Nearly 1,000 Arrests
intermediate.brief: Hundreds of thousands of people took part in mass demonstrations across France on Saturday. While many marches were calm, violent conflict erupted between protesters and riot police in Paris. Some protesters built makeshift barricades and threw projectiles at officers, while masked youths smashed windows. In response, law enforcement used water cannon to disperse crowds in several cities. Despite the violence, officials have so far managed to avoid the extreme disorder seen last weekend. Officials stated that nearly 1,000 arrests were made following the protests. Two demonstrators explained that they feel abandoned by the government. Similar issues have triggered mass protests in several other European cities. These recent events follow weeks of escalating tension over rising fuel prices.

advanced.headline: Mass Protests and Clashes Grip France Ahead of Elections
advanced.brief: French officials confirmed that nearly 1,000 arrests were made as hundreds of thousands of people participated in another day of protests across the nation. Approximately 70,000 police officers were deployed to prevent the latest protests from descending into the kind of chaos that previously saw officers outnumbered. Officials have so far managed to avoid rioting and looting on the scale seen last weekend, averting the worst scenes of disorder. Furthermore, President Emmanuel Macron decreed that only demonstrations organised by recognised trade unions would be legally permitted. Despite these measures, the interior minister noted that several thousand radical activists gathered at the rear of the march. Tensions rose as police baton-charged groups of masked youths who were smashing windows and pelting officers with various objects. In the southern port of Marseille, rubbish bins were set ablaze and metal sheets were used to block streets. Meanwhile, authorities in Lyon utilised non-lethal grenades to scatter a crowd that had reportedly gathered in an area deemed off-limits by the local prefecture. In Barcelona, over 100 people were arrested after a student protest resulted in what local authorities described as gratuitous violence. The continuing unrest comes ahead of presidential elections in six months' time, with leading contenders levelling the blame directly at Macron.
